summary: A Knizia area-control and tile-laying game where players place tokens along rivers and near cities in ancient Mesopotamia to gain influence and score based on shared territories. It's a lean, tightly designed game with a sudden-death ending that rewards careful positioning over long-term engine building.
praised: elegant, tight Knizia design with meaningful decisions
quick sudden-death ending keeps tension high
criticised: can feel dry or abstract despite the theme
sudden ending can catch players off guard
less well-known so harder to find opponents familiar with it

interaction.detail: Players place pieces on a shared hex map where majority in each region determines who scores, so placements are constantly contesting the same spaces. There is very little private player board; almost all the meaningful state is shared on the map.

sources: noble-chain points when a city is surrounded (2 pts per matching noble)
running city-count bonus paid to every city owner each time a new city is claimed
Ziggurat adjacency points (1 per ziggurat touched)
Ziggurat majority bonus cards (one-off 10 pts or ongoing ability)
scoring.how_you_win: Place noble, farmer, and clan tiles to win majority control of cities, gather points around Ziggurats, and fill Crop Fields, scoring points continuously as cities close and tiles are placed; the game ends the instant a player runs out of clan tokens or the board runs out of cities, and the highest accumulated total wins.
